Second, we construct a Bayesian framework to constrain the viewing angle by matching the FRADO-based $R_{\rm BLR}$ to the measured H$β$ lags of 151 AGN from Wang & Woo (2024). We successfully reproduce the slope and intrinsic scatter of the observed $R_{\rm BLR}$-$L_{5100}$ relation, finding that the inferred viewing angles are broadly consistent with the estimates from dynamical modeling of velocity-resolved reverberation data, albeit with substantial scatter. As the observed H$β$ time lag and line velocity depend on the viewing angle, the black hole mass ($M_{\rm BH}$) calibrated from our work is typically larger than the reverberation-mapping estimates using an average virial factor. Our results provide a physically motivated interpretation of the $R_{\rm BLR}$-$L_{5100}$ relation and the systematic uncertainties in reverberation and single-epoch $M_{\rm BH}$ estimates.

entries.title: The Evolution of the Circumgalactic Medium after a starburst in DESI Post-Starburst Galaxies
entries.abstract: We present a statistical study of the cool circumgalactic medium (CGM) around massive post-starburst galaxies, traced by Mg II $λ\lambda2796,2803$ absorption in background quasar spectra from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 2. Cross-matching ~1.98 million quasar sightlines with luminous red galaxies at $0.4 < z < 0.76$ with stellar masses between $10.6 < \log_{10}(M_*/\mathrm{M}_\odot) < 12$ yields ~143 million galaxy-quasar pairs, 50-60 times more per impact-parameter bin than our previous SDSS-based analysis. We stack the Mg II absorption as a function of projected separation and classify the foreground galaxies using mean-field independent component analysis (MFICA), further subdividing the post-starburst population into sub-samples ordered by time since the starburst. The mean Mg II equivalent width declines with impact parameter for every class. Post-starburst galaxies show the strongest absorption of any spectral class, reaching $W_{\rm MgII} = 1.58 \pm 0.32$ Å within 71 kpc, well above star-forming ($0.69 \pm 0.15$ Å) and quiescent ($0.22 \pm 0.05$ Å) galaxies of comparable stellar mass at the same projected separation. Within the post-starburst phase the absorption profile evolves systematically: the youngest systems show the highest, most centrally concentrated absorption and the steepest radial decline, whereas progressively older systems show weaker inner absorption and enhanced absorption at intermediate radii (~300-1000 kpc). Independent Bagpipes star-formation-history fitting confirms that this ordering corresponds to an ageing sequence. We interpret this evolution as the outward redistribution of cool gas expelled by feedback-driven winds, consistent with characteristic outflow velocities of a few hundred km s$^{-1}$, with a residual inner cool-gas reservoir persisting throughout the post-starburst phase.

entries.title: SN 2025dys: A luminous supernova explosion from a partially stripped helium star
entries.abstract: We present well-sampled multi-band imaging and low- to medium-resolution spectroscopic observations of the early-discovered Type~II supernova (SN)~2025dys. The photometric evolution exhibits a rise time of $\sim$\,18 days ($r$ band) and a rapid decline transitioning to the radioactive decay tail at $\sim$\,70 days. SN~2025dys is among the high-luminosity events with a peak pseudo-bolometric luminosity of $L_{\rm opt}=8.57\times10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. Early X-ray emission was identified, displaying a luminosity of $7.55\times10^{40}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. The observational investigation points to a dense, hydrogen-rich circumstellar medium with a mass of $M_{\rm CSM}\approx0.5$--$0.7\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$, suggesting a partially stripped, hydrogen-poor inner ejecta with a relatively low mass of $M_{\rm ej}\approx2.5\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$. The explosion possessed a kinetic energy of $E_{\rm k}\approx0.3\text{--}0.5$~foe and yielded a synthesized nickel mass of $M_{\rm Ni}\approx0.042_{-0.011}^{+0.012}\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$. These physical parameters indicate an extreme mass-loss episode before the explosion, characterized by a high mass-loss rate of $\dot{M} \gtrsim 0.01\,\mathrm{M_\odot\,yr^{-1}}$. SN~2025dys represents a stripped progenitor, intrinsically resembling a Type~IIb or even a Type~Ib SN, that exploded within a dense, hydrogen-rich circumstellar environment.

entries.title: The Pristine Survey. XXX. Mapping substructures in the inner and outer halo with blue horizontal branch stars
entries.abstract: Blue horizontal branch (BHB) stars serve as good standard candles and kinematic tracers of the Milky Way halo. The halo displays various overdensities and kinematical substructures of different shapes and sizes. Our objective is to investigate the substructure in three dimensions and the bulk motion of the halo up to distances well exceeding the limit of the Gaia parallaxes. We selected BHB stars in the $\left(u-CaHK\right) _ 0$-$(g-r) _ 0$ colour-colour diagram with a hierarchical Bayesian mixture model of three populations: BHB stars, blue straggler stars, and outliers. Using $CaHK$ photometry derived from Gaia XP spectra and the Pristine survey, we provide both a shallow and a deep catalogue of BHB stars of 7,057 and 8,824 stars, respectively, where the deep catalogue is restricted to the deeper Pristine footprint compared to the shallower with Gaia XP. Using the shallow catalogue, we trace to larger distances 6D substructures identified earlier within a 2.5 kpc from the Sun, including accepted populations; namely, Gaia-Enceladus, Thamnos, Helmi streams, Sequoia, and other smaller halo substructures such as ED-3, ED-4, and ED-6. The deep catalogue provides reliable distance measurements for a more detailed 3D mapping of the Sagittarius stream and of the Pisces Overdensity. We add new candidate BHB stars with line-of-sight velocities to existing catalogues and confirm previously reported differences between the northern and southern Galactic hemispheres, likely due to the infall of the Large Magellanic Cloud. This research demonstrates that probabilistic photometric classification can effectively identify distant candidate BHB stars, and can provide catalogues of these stars that enhance our understanding of the 3D and 6D structures in the halo of the Milky Way.

entries.title: Long-term variability of the 35-day cycle in Her X-1
entries.abstract: Her X-1 is an eclipsing X-ray binary system consisting of an accreting neutron star and an optical component HZ Her. In addition to the 1.24-s X-ray pulsations and the 1.7-d orbital period, the system also shows a 35-day X-ray variability related to the precessional motion of a tilted and twisted accretion disk around the neutron star. The long-term persistence of the 35-day X-ray variability suggests the presence of a stable clock mechanism, most likely free precession of the magnetized neutron star. We have studied the long-term behavior of the 35-day cycle of Her X-1 using all available CGRO/BATSE, RXTE/ASM, Swift/BAT, Fermi/GBM, MAXI data and archival turn-on moments of the 35-day cycle spanning more than 50 years. We have used a sliding-window averaged X-ray phase light curve and the classical O-C (observed minus calculated) diagram for individual 35-day turn-ons to inspect the long-term trends of the O-C diagram. The O-C diagram demonstrates two similar parabolic trends separated by an anomalous low state (ALS) of the source suggesting a secular decrease in the 35-d precession period with $\dot P_\text{35} =(-1.3\pm0.2)\times10^{-5} \,\mathrm{~s\,s}^{-1}$ and $\dot P_\text{35} =(-4.7\pm0.1)\times10^{-5} \,\mathrm{~s\,s}^{-1}$ before and after the ALS, respectively. We conclude that the decay of the 35-day period as inferred from the O-C analysis can be interpreted in terms of the direct relationship between the change of the precessional period of the accretion disk to the long-term decrease of the period of the free precessional neutron star - due to continued accumulation of accreted matter.

entries.title: Gamma-Ray Emission from LS 5039: A 30-500 GeV Excess and Phase-Resolved Broadband Spectral Modeling
entries.abstract: LS~5039 is a well-studied $γ$-ray binary exhibiting strong orbital modulation from GeV to TeV energies. We present a phase-resolved analysis of 17.3~yr of \textit{Fermi}-LAT observations and identify an additional $γ$-ray excess in the $\sim30$--$500$~GeV at a significance of $\sim7.9σ$. The phase-resolved spectra show pronounced orbital dependence above $\sim10$~GeV, with the inferior-conjunction more complex than the superior-conjunction. To investigate the broadband spectral energy distribution, we combine the \textit{Fermi}-LAT spectra with published H.E.S.S.\ and HAWC measurements and compare purely leptonic and lepto-hadronic models using the Bayesian information criterion. In both intervals, relativistic-Maxwellian and magnetospheric components dominate below $\sim10$~GeV, while shock-accelerated electrons account for much of the GeV--TeV continuum. The purely leptonic fits leave residuals at $30$--$500$~GeV and underpredict the HAWC measurements above $\sim100$~TeV. In the local one-zone intrabinary shock apex model, synchrotron cooling and Klein-Nishina suppression make the ultra-high-energy emission difficult to reproduce, although more complex leptonic scenarios remain possible. Adding a phenomenological proton component improves the broadband description, with stronger relative support during superior-conjunction than inferior-conjunction. However, the proton parameters remain weakly constrained and the fast-escape hadronic interpretation is energetically challenging, so a hadronic origin is not uniquely established. Future high-sensitivity, phase-resolved observations at multi-TeV and ultra-high energies will be required to test this interpretation.

entries.title: Inferring dominant acceleration mechanisms using the longitudinal spread of solar particle intensities: 28 May 2021 event
entries.abstract: Solar energetic particles (SEPs) are typically accelerated during solar eruptions and propagate along magnetic field lines in the inner heliosphere. These eruptions include shock waves driven by coronal mass ejections (CMEs) and magnetic reconnection in solar flares. Disentangling these source mechanisms within the measurements has been a long-standing problem for space physics researchers. Since spacecraft rarely reach the acceleration regions close to the Sun, measured SEP intensities reflect a combination of particle acceleration and interplanetary transport. The method used in this study attempts to identify which of the two main acceleration processes is more dominant for specific particle energies and species in a standalone event. Through this approach, we aim to better identify the signatures associated with these two acceleration phenomena and recognize similar behaviors in measurements with transport effects. This study characterizes the longitudinal spread of the SEP event on 28 May 2021 by fitting Gaussian curves at regular time intervals to particle intensities as a function of spacecraft position. This evolution offers unprecedented detail compared to earlier peak-focused studies, which were also limited to only three observers, while we now benefit from a novel fleet. To support the interpretation of the evolving profiles, we use a 2D SEP transport model to test if the evolution of the SEP distribution can also be caused by interplanetary effects. For this event, we find that the particle distribution of 0.1 MeV electrons remains static, while for 14 and 32 MeV protons, the distribution grows and moves to the west. We suggest that the CME-driven shock is the dominant source for protons, and that the flare is the dominant source only for the studied 0.1 MeV electrons. Interplanetary transport processes could also be contributing to the moving particle distributions.

entries.title: Decay of space plasma turbulence downstream of bow shocks: MMS magnetosheath unbiased campaign observations
entries.abstract: Turbulence properties in the solar wind change with increasing heliospheric distance. Observations from different missions have shown how spectral indices converge towards a $f^{-5/3}$ spectrum in the inertial range as the solar wind reaches one astronomical unit, and how the cascade rate decays as the plasma moves away from the Sun. We evaluate whether these properties display similar trends in a smaller astrophysical system, that of a planetary magnetosheath. Using data from the 2023 Magnetospheric Multiscale (MMS) unbiased magnetosheath campaign, we determine the evolution of the spectral indices and the cascade rate along 15 inbound magnetosheath crossings. WIND observations permitted to monitor the state of the solar wind during the campaign and allowed to study the impact of the upstream plasma conditions on the evolution of the cascade rate downstream the bow shock. Our results show an increase of the cascade rate between two to three orders of magnitude after the plasma crosses the bow shock into the magnetosheath. Once in the magnetosheath, turbulence develops with increasing distance to the bow shock in a way similar to solar wind observations, despite the smaller size of the system. Incompressible Hall-MHD scaling-law estimates of the cascade rate show a clear power-law decay of the cascade rate in the magnetosheath, particularly for the cases with upstream slow wind. This suggests that the way energy is injected into the system plays a role in the decay of turbulence as the plasma moves away from the bow shock.

entries.title: First Light with the Dark100 Array of PANOSETI Telescopes at Palomar Observatory
entries.abstract: Dark100 is the first phase of an extensive array of Panoramic SETI (PANOSETI) telescopes at Palomar Observatory, California. PANOSETI telescopes are small, 0.5-m Fresnel lens telescopes instrumented with 1024-pixel silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) cameras. The telescopes were originally designed to search for ultra-fast optical transients, but they also function as cost-effective imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (IACTs). Dark100 will use seven of these widely separated IACTs to map the ultra-high-energy (UHE) gamma-ray sources on the Galactic Plane at high resolution. Dark100 will also leverage the IACT technique to search for evidence of ultra-heavy dark matter in a mass range that extends beyond 100 TeV. Deployment of the first four telescopes and enclosures was completed in December 2025, and commissioning of the next three is scheduled to finish by the end of 2026. The array has so far collected more than 100 hours of 3-telescope data on sources including the Crab Nebula and Markarian 421. Here we present the current status of Dark100.

entries.title: The multiple origins of spurs in stellar streams: a challenge for dark matter diagnostics
entries.abstract: Spurs along stellar streams are often interpreted as signatures of interactions with dark matter subhalos, and thus have been proposed as diagnostics on the clustering and nature of dark matter. Although galactic baryonic components could play similar roles as gravitational perturbers of streams, the possible signatures they leave and the degeneracy with subhalos have been overlooked. In this paper, we analyse simulations of streams experiencing disruptions by dark matter subhalos, a galactic bar, and a galaxy merger. Although spurs are more frequently found to be induced by the galaxy merger, the spurs originating from all these processes are morphologically similar. Therefore, such morphological features should not be used alone to characterise the mechanism of their origin, nor to constrain the nature of dark matter.

entries.title: A multi-wavelength view of PSR J0437-4715 with NICER and other missions: Radius measurements from far-ultraviolet to hard X-ray pulse profile modeling
entries.abstract: We report updated mass and radius measurements for the millisecond pulsar PSR J0437-4715 obtained with pulse profile modeling of the emission from the far-ultraviolet to the hard X-rays. Using an extended 2.56 Ms Neutron Star Interior Composition ExploreR (NICER) dataset together with XMM-Newton, Nuclear Spectroscopic Telescope ARray and Hubble Space Telescope observations, we perform Bayesian inference with models describing the thermal emission from hot spots of increasing complexities, together with the rest of the warm NS surface, as well as the non-thermal emission component represented by a phase-dependent (pulsed) power-law. With this comprehensive model and broadband data set, as well as radio timing priors on the mass, distance and inclination, our headline result for PSR J0437-4715 led to a mass M = 1.377(-0.034)(+0.038) Msun and an equatorial radius Req = 11.35(-0.39)(+0.40) km, one of the narrowest measurements of Req from NICER observations of millisecond pulsars. The geometric configuration favors a non-antipodal hot spot distribution, as noted in previous analyses of this pulsar. When combined with recent measurements of M and Req of other pulsars, the tight constraints from PSR J0437-4715 further reduce the allowed range of the dense matter equation of state, excluding those that predict radii above 12.0 km (at the 68% level) for all NS masses.

entries.title: Bar likelihood in local galaxies: the joint role of stellar mass, morphology and environment
entries.abstract: We investigate how the likelihood of hosting a stellar bar depends on both intrinsic galaxy properties and environment, using a volume-limited sample of central and satellite galaxies from the NASA-Sloan Atlas, spanning isolated systems, low- and high-richness groups, and massive haloes, complemented with halo-based environmental information and probabilistic morphology. Using probabilistic bar identification, we quantify the bar likelihood as a function of stellar mass, colour, morphology, halo mass, and cluster-centric distance. We find that stellar mass and morphology are the galaxy properties most associated with the bar likelihood. At fixed morphology, the probability of hosting a bar increases with stellar mass, particularly for late-type galaxies. At the same time, morphology strongly modulates the overall incidence of bars, with early-type galaxies displaying systematically lower probabilities than late-type systems across the stellar mass range. Environmental trends are observed, including halo mass and cluster-centric distance, but these trends largely reflect the morphological composition of the galaxy population. In particular, the decrease in bar likelihood towards the centres of massive haloes reflects the increasing fraction of early-type galaxies, consistent with the morphology-density relation, rather than a direct environmental suppression of bars. Our residual analysis finds no statistically significant residual dependence on halo mass or normalized cluster-centric distance after accounting for stellar mass and morphology, within the sensitivity of this sample. Overall, our results show that stellar mass and morphology are the main factors associated with bar likelihood.

entries.title: Collisional excitation of HMgC$_3$N by He: rate coefficients and astrophysical implications
entries.abstract: Reliable collisional data are essential for interpreting the rotational emission of HMgC$_3$N under the non-equilibrium conditions of molecular clouds. We investigate the rotational excitation and de-excitation of HMgC$_3$N induced by collisions with He, combining \textit{ab initio} calculations with quantum scattering theory. A two-dimensional potential energy surface (PES) for HMgC$_3$N--He was constructed using the CCSD(T)-F12A method in conjunction with the aug-cc-pVTZ basis set. Quantum close-coupling (CC) calculation were then performed to obtain state-to-state integral cross sections and temperature-dependent rate coefficients for rotational transitions with $Δj=\pm1$, $\pm2$, and $\pm3$, covering rotational levels up to $j=20$ and temperatures from $3$ to $50$~K. The rate coefficients exhibit a clear propensity for $Δj=\pm2$ transitions. The resulting collisional data were incorporated into radiative transfer modelling to constrain the physical conditions and column density of HMgC$_3$N from its observed spectral line emission. A $χ^2$ minimization yields a best-fitting H$_2$ volume density of $n(\mathrm{H}_2)=1.233\times10^5~\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$ and column density of $N(\mathrm{HMgC}_3\mathrm{N})=1.831\times10^{12}~\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$. The derived column density is in approximate agreement with the observational estimate of $(3.0\pm0.6)\times10^{12}~\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$. These results provide new collisional data for non-LTE studies of HMgC$_3$N and support a more realistic treatment of its rotational excitation and radiative transfer in molecular clouds.

entries.title: The Unusual X-ray Spectrum of R Mon
entries.abstract: The optically obscured young star R Mon illuminates Hubble's Variable Nebula and has historically been classified as an intermediate mass pre-main sequence Herbig Be star. We present Chandra observations of R Mon revealing a hard X-ray source viewed through high absorption from circumstellar gas known to be present from previous CO observations. The X-ray spectrum is characterized by line emission from the He-like Fe K complex (6.7 keV) tracing very hot plasma and fluorescent Fe emission (6.4 keV) from cold gas near the star that is irradiated by hard X-rays. Low-level variability on a timescale of less than one day is detected, but no large impulsive flares. The hot plasma and variability cannot be explained by shock models and magnetically confined plasma is inferred. The hard X-ray spectrum of R Mon does not resemble the soft spectra of prototypical Herbig stars but is remarkably similar to some class I protostars such as NGC 2071-IRS 1. As judged by its X-ray and infrared properties, we conclude that R Mon is a class I protostar and thus provides a rare snapshot of an emergent intermediate mass star enveloped in X-ray irradiated gas and dust.

entries.title: The 943 MHz radio-SFR relation of nearby galaxies observed with ASKAP
entries.abstract: We investigate the integrated 943 MHz radio-infrared and radio-star-formation-rate (SFR) relations of 875 nearby galaxies within $D<50$ Mpc using public Australian SKA Pathfinder (ASKAP) observations. After excluding galaxies with identified or candidate AGN activity, 594 galaxies remain in the AGN-cleaned sample. We used Bayesian errors-in-variables models that account for measurement uncertainties, intrinsic scatter, and correlated distance errors. The AGN-cleaned radio-infrared relation is nearly linear, $L_{ν,943}\propto L_{ν,\mathrm{W4}}^{1.09\pm0.02}$, with an orthogonal intrinsic scatter of $0.21\pm0.01$ dex, and is tighter than the AGN-host relation. For 592 AGN-cleaned galaxies, the radio-SFR relation is approximately linear, $L_{ν,943}\propto{\rm SFR}^{1.02\pm0.02}$, with an intrinsic scatter of $0.25\pm0.01$ dex. Semi-calorimetric models reveal positive secondary dependences on stellar mass, $γ=0.09\pm0.03$, and rotation velocity, $δ=0.24\pm0.08$. The consistency between these two secondary trends suggests that the galaxy gravitational potential may weakly regulate CRE confinement and synchrotron-radiation efficiency. Our results provide an integrated 943 MHz radio-SFR calibration for nearby galaxies and show that, although radio luminosity scales nearly proportionally with SFR on average, weak secondary dependences on galaxy properties remain.

entries.title: Stellar Kinematics and Molecular Gas toward NGC 6357: An Overlooked Earlier Stellar Generation
entries.abstract: We investigate past star formation in NGC 6357 using Gaia DR3 astrometry and Three-mm Ultimate Mopra Milky Way Survey (ThrUMMS) $^{12}$CO($J=1$--0) data. A Hierarchical Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (HDBSCAN) search independently recovers the previously cataloged cluster G352.8+0.6 in addition to Pismis 24, G353.1+0.6, and G353.2+0.6. Isochrone fitting yields an age of $7.9^{+1.5}_{-1.4}$ Myr for G352.8+0.6, compared with approximately 1--3 Myr for the three young clusters. Assuming constant relative plane-of-sky motion, a linear traceback places G352.8+0.6 closest to their reference center approximately 1.8 Myr ago, comparable to their inferred ages. The $+2$ km s$^{-1}$ CO component overlaps G352.8+0.6 in projection and shows localized depressions in integrated intensity around three spectroscopically identified massive stars belonging to G352.8+0.6. The $-4$ and $+2$ km s$^{-1}$ components show complementary projected distributions and intermediate-velocity CO emission in position--velocity space. Assuming that the $+2$ km s$^{-1}$ component was physically associated with G352.8+0.6 and shared its transverse motion, our principal interpretation is that the two molecular structures interacted around the epoch indicated by the stellar traceback, approximately 1.8 Myr ago. The resulting gas compression may have contributed to the recent episode of clustered and high-mass star formation in NGC 6357 and to the formation of Shell A, which subsequent stellar feedback may have reshaped.

entries.title: Current Sheets and Magnetic Reconnection statistics by Solar Orbiter at few to tens of Ion Inertial Lengths I: Energy Dissipation
entries.abstract: In this work, we study the turbulent origin of ion-scale Current Sheets (CSs) and the dissipation of energy via magnetic reconnection. We analyze 103 hours of high-cadence (4 samples/s) in-situ ion data from Solar Orbiter, collected between July 2020 and September 2022. We apply an automatic detection algorithm that finds current sheets (CSs) of thickness (length in the normal direction, $λ$) near the ion inertial length ($δ_i$), and classifies them as Alfvénic or reconnecting. We compile a catalog of 974 CSs of thickness in the range of few to 90 ion inertial lengths, of which 53 contain an ion reconnection jet. We estimate that Solar Orbiter spends $\sim 1 \%$ of the dwell time inside a CS of few to 90 $δ_i$ thickness, and 0.06\% inside a reconnecting CS of the same thickness range. By comparing these results with previous studies we estimate that the abundance of CSs and of Reconnecting CSs evolves with heliocentric distance ($r$) as $r^{-0.9}$ and $r^{-1.5}$, respectively. We estimate that magnetic reconnection dissipates $ε_{rec}\sim 30 \hspace{5pt} \text{J} \text{kg}^{-1} \text{s}^{-1},$ in the $\sim 1 - 40$ $δ_i$ scale-range, by assessing the amount of plasma that interacts with a reconnection exhaust. We show how the dissipation of turbulence energy cascade by magnetic reconnection at scales smaller than 90 $δ_i$ is more effective closer to the Sun, and decays as $r^{-3.6}$. The current density of Alfvénic CSs thicker than the ion inertial length presents scale invariance, obeying $J_0/J_A=0.9(λ/2δ_i)^{-0.71}$, suggesting that CSs generated locally from solar wind turbulence.

entries.title: Formation of Micron-sized Presolar Graphite Grains in Low-energy Supernova Ejecta
entries.abstract: Presolar graphite grains with supernova isotopic signatures provide direct evidence that large graphite grains formed in supernova ejecta. However, theoretical calculations of dust formation in supernovae have typically predicted graphite grains smaller than $0.1\,{\rm μm}$, leaving unclear the physical conditions required to form those grains with radii of order $1\,{\rm μm}$. We systematically investigate graphite nucleation and growth in expanding supernova ejecta by varying the explosion energy, ejecta mass, initial ejecta radius, and ejected $^{56}$Ni mass. We use a simplified one-zone model that follows the temperature and density evolution including adiabatic cooling, radiative cooling, and heating by radioactive nickel. We show that the final graphite grain size is mainly determined by the product of the mass density of atomic carbon available for grain growth and the local cooling timescale, both evaluated at a reference temperature of $2000\,{\rm K}$. Our models show that graphite growth is favored by lower explosion energy, larger ejecta mass, and smaller initial ejecta radius, which keep the gas denser near the graphite-condensation temperature. When radioactive heating and radiative cooling are included, explosions with $E_{\rm exp}\sim10^{50}\,{\rm erg}$ and $M_{\rm Ni}\lesssim10^{-3}\,M_\odot$ can form $1$-$10\,μ{\rm m}$ graphite grains in the ejected helium layer or carbon-oxygen core, whereas $E_{\rm exp}\sim10^{51}\,{\rm erg}$ models do not. These results suggest that micron-sized presolar supernova graphite preferentially forms in faint-supernova-like explosions with low explosion energies, little ejected nickel, and helium layer or carbon-oxygen core ejecta.

entries.title: Nova V1674 Her as a fast magnetic rotator
entries.abstract: We report on the results of our XMM-Newton and NuSTAR campaign targeting V1674 Her in October 2023. These observations were timed to investigate the post-nova quiescent state 28 months after the 2021 outburst, although the optical luminosity was still slowly declining. The X-ray spectra are well-modeled by a multi-temperature thermal plasma. While in the best fit temperature we find that the highest plasma temperature is indicative of a massive white dwarf ($M_{\text{WD}} \approx 1.35 M_\odot$), we caution that there is a degeneracy between the plasma temperature and the metallicity in the spectral fit, hindering a definitive constraint. Alternatively, the continuum can be phenomenologically described by a Comptonized component, although this model neglects the thermal bremsstrahlung component. Timing analysis reveals a stable 501.31 $\pm$ 0.19 s modulation in the post-quiescent phase, whose amplitude diminishes with increasing energy; this is quite typical in intermediate polars (IP). The phase alignment between the quiescent and early post-outburst Chandra spin-folded light curves suggests that the soft X-ray emission originates from the same polar regions, which quickly re-established accretion following the eruption. V1674 Her belongs to a growing class of novae that are also IPs, and is one of four in which the modulation with rotation was observed during the outburst supersoft X-ray phase. We propose that the fast rise in outburst was due to a fast or centrifugal magnetic rotator wind, causing rapid mass loss instead of the commonly assumed radiation pressure wind.

The contrastive-learning branch projects the gravitational-wave and optical representations into a shared embedding space and uses a supervised contrastive objective with a time-compatibility term to favour physically plausible pairs. analysis.reason: This work performs an unprecedented multi-wavelength pulse profile modeling (PPM) of the nearest millisecond pulsar PSR J0437-4715 combining HST, NICER, XMM-Newton, and NuSTAR datasets to obtain the tightest neutron star radius and equation of state constraints to date.
analysis.result: Using the ST+PDT+EL+PL surface emission configuration, the headline PPM inference yields an equatorial radius of $R_{\rm eq} = 11.35_{-0.39}^{+0.40}\,\mathrm{km}$ (or $R_{\rm eq} = 11.345_{-0.388}^{+0.399}\,\mathrm{km}$) and a mass of $M = 1.377_{-0.034}^{+0.038}\,M_{\odot}$. The whole-surface warm emission has an effective temperature in the stellar frame of $\log_{10}(T_{\rm else}\,[\mathrm{K}]) = 5.451 \pm 0.008$ ($T_{\rm else} = (2.82 \pm 0.05) \times 10^{5}\,\mathrm{K}$), translating to an observer at infinity to $T_{\rm else}^{\infty} = T_{\rm else}/(1+z) = (2.26 \pm 0.03) \times 10^{5}\,\mathrm{K}$ via the gravitational redshift $1+z = \left(1 - \frac{2GM}{R_{\rm eq}c^2}\right)^{-1/2}$, with observed flux scaling as $F \propto (R_{\rm eq}^{\infty}/d)^2 \sigma (T_{\rm else}^{\infty})^4$. The pulsed non-thermal power-law component exhibits photon index $\Gamma_{\rm PL} = 1.310_{-0.061}^{+0.054}$ and pulsed amplitude $A_{\rm PL} = 0.684_{-0.057}^{+0.059}$. At the 95% credibility level, the upper limit of the neutron star radius is reduced by $\approx 0.4\text{--}0.6\,\mathrm{km}$, yielding inferred radius at $1.4\,M_{\odot}$ of $R_{1.4} = 11.52_{-0.50}^{+0.66}\,\mathrm{km}$ (piecewise polytrope) and $11.48_{-0.52}^{+0.61}\,\mathrm{km}$ (speed of sound), ruling out stiff EOSs with $R > 12.0\,\mathrm{km}$ at 68% credibility.
analysis.problem: Previous radius inferences of PSR J0437-4715 suffered from strong degeneracies between the pulsed non-thermal magnetospheric power-law tail, the soft thermal hot spots, and the diffuse warm stellar surface. Without joint far-UV (HST) and hard X-ray (NuSTAR) coverage, the non-thermal normalization and whole-surface emission were unconstrained, leading to divergent radius posteriors ranging from $\sim 7.9\,\mathrm{km}$ up to $\sim 14.1\,\mathrm{km}$.
analysis.method: The authors perform multi-wavelength pulse profile modeling within an extended X-PSI Bayesian inference framework over $0.007\text{--}16.0\,\mathrm{keV}$, integrating $2.56\,\mathrm{Ms}$ of NICER XTI data, $113\,\mathrm{ks}$ of XMM-Newton EPIC MOS data, $221\,\mathrm{ks}$ of NuSTAR FPM data ($3.0\text{--}16.0\,\mathrm{keV}$), and HST STIS far-UV spectroscopy ($1150\text{--}1700\,\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$). The likelihood couples a modified Gaussian log-likelihood for HST STIS fluxes $\mathcal{L}(\theta,\mathbf{B})=\sum_{i,k}\left[\frac{(c_{ik}(\theta)-d_{ik}+B_{i}T_{\rm exp}\int_{\phi_{k}}d\phi)^2}{\sigma_{ik}^2}+\ln(2\pi\sigma_{ik}^2)\right]$ with Poisson likelihoods for X-ray timing data. assumptions: The warm unheated stellar surface emits as a partially ionized hydrogen atmosphere (NSXHp) at uniform effective temperature $T_{\rm else}$ over the region outside the hot spots.

analysis.reason: The paper investigates the physical conditions required to form micron-sized presolar graphite grains in supernova ejecta, providing key scaling relations linking grain sizes to explosion energy, ejecta mass, progenitor radius, and nickel heating.
analysis.result: In Ni-free ejecta undergoing matter-dominated adiabatic expansion, the final graphite grain radius scales analytically as $r_{\rm gr,final} \simeq 615\,\mu\mathrm{m}\,(E_{\rm exp}/10^{48}\,\mathrm{erg})^{-3/2}\,(M_{\rm ej}/5\,M_\odot)^{5/2}\,(R_0/10^{12}\,\mathrm{cm})^{-2}\,(X'_{\rm C}/3\times 10^{-3})$, governed by the local key parameter combination $X'_{\rm C}\rho_{2000}\tau_{\rm cool,2000} \propto X'_{\rm C}E_{\rm exp}^{-3/2}M_{\rm ej}^{5/2}R_0^{-2}$. Micron-sized grains ($r_{\rm gr} \gtrsim 1\,\mu\mathrm{m}$) require low explosion energy ($E_{\rm exp} \lesssim 10^{49}\text{--}10^{50}\,\mathrm{erg}$), massive ejecta, and negligible radioactive $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ heating, as $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ heating delays dust condensation until the ejecta expands to much lower densities, suppressing final grain radii below $0.1\,\mu\mathrm{m}$.
analysis.reading_entry: 4.2 Analytical estimates of the grain size
analysis.problem: Presolar graphite grains extracted from meteorites exhibit supernova isotopic signatures and reach sizes $\gtrsim 1\,\mu\mathrm{m}$, whereas standard core-collapse supernova models ($E_{\rm exp} \sim 10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$, $M_{\rm ej} \sim 10\,M_\odot$, $M_{\rm Ni} \sim 0.01\text{--}0.1\,M_\odot$) typically predict graphite grain sizes below $0.1\,\mu\mathrm{m}$.
analysis.method: A spherical, uniformly expanding one-zone ejecta dynamics model coupled to an energy equation including radioactive $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}\rightarrow{}^{56}\mathrm{Co}\rightarrow{}^{56}\mathrm{Fe}$ decay heating $\dot{Q}$, $p\,dV$ work, and radiative cooling. Dust formation is calculated using classical homogeneous nucleation theory for carbon monomers and moment equations $dK_j^{(\ell)}/dt$ coupled to key species depletion, with analytical scaling relations derived for the matter-dominated adiabatic limit ($T \propto \rho^{2/3}$) at the reference condensation temperature $T = 2000\,\mathrm{K}$.
assumptions: Constant carbon sticking probability $\alpha_{\rm C} = 1$ and pre-set effective carbon mass fraction $X'_{\rm C}$ assuming molecular CO formation locks up equal parts of carbon and oxygen without solving explicit time-dependent chemical networks.
limits: Calculations do not resolve the multi-dimensional density and composition structure, clumping, or radioactive chemical destruction within real supernova ejecta.
citation_leads: Formation of Micron-sized Presolar Graphite Grains in Low-energy Supernova Ejecta: “Presolar graphite grains with supernova isotopic signatures provide direct evidence that large graphite grains formed in supernova ejecta.”
3.1 Overview of nucleation theory: “In cooling and expanding ejecta, atoms and molecules in the gas phase form condensation nuclei, which subsequently grow into dust grains.”

4.2 Analytical estimates of the grain size: “The numerical results thus reveal an approximately single-valued relation between $X^{\prime}_{\rm C}\rho_{2000}\tau_{\rm cool,2000}$ and the final grain size over the explored range of Ni-free adiabatic models.”

4.4 The effect of Ni heating: “Radioactive heating lengthens $\tau_{{\rm cool},2000}$, but it also delays condensation while the ejecta continue to expand, lowering $\rho_{2000}$ by orders of magnitude”
5.3 Caveat: “The present one-zone calculations identify conditions favorable for graphite formation, but do not resolve the density and composition structure, clumping, or mixing within the ejecta.”
Appendix B Effective growth window: “Because the nucleation rate depends exponentially on the supersaturation ratio, this temperature width is much smaller than unity in logarithmic temperature.”
analysis.research_progress: Unifies grain growth physics via the dimensionless collision-to-saturation timescale parameter and maps it directly onto bulk supernova observables, establishing that low-energy ($E_{\rm exp} \ll 10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$), $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$-poor core-collapse supernovae are the requisite stellar environment for synthesizing micron-sized presolar graphite grains.

analysis.reason: Investigates the quiescent post-outburst state of the ultrafast nova and intermediate polar candidate V1674 Her with joint NuSTAR and XMM-Newton observations, demonstrating magnetic field survival and constraining WD shock energetics.
analysis.result: The quiescent X-ray spectrum is consistent with multi-temperature shock emission with a high maximum temperature $kT_{\max} \ge 69\text{ keV}$, yielding a massive white dwarf estimate of $M_{\text{WD}} = 1.26_{-0.56}^{+0.11}\,M_\odot$ (or $\approx 1.35\,M_\odot$). Timing analysis yields a spin period $P = 501.31 \pm 0.19\text{ s}$ (and $501.35 \pm 0.19\text{ s}$) with energy-dependent modulation (pulse fraction dropping from $60\%$ to $47\%$) and strict phase alignment of pulse minima between the 2021 outburst and 2024 quiescence.

analysis.problem: Uncovering the origin of the hard X-ray emission (thermal accretion shock vs. Comptonized column), constraining the white dwarf mass, and explaining the rapid optical rise and early $\gamma$-ray emission in the presence of strong magnetic rotation.
analysis.method: Quasi-simultaneous XMM-Newton (0.3–10 keV) and NuSTAR (3–40 keV) spectral modeling using multi-temperature plasma (`mkcflow`), Comptonization (`compTT`), and magnetized post-shock accretion column (`ipolar30kK`) models, combined with Lomb-Scargle and Phase Dispersion Minimization (PDM) timing analyses.
assumptions: The large-scale dipolar magnetic field structure survives the nova thermonuclear runaway and anchors accretion and burning at the magnetic poles.
limits: A severe degeneracy between high shock temperature $kT_{\max}$ and sub-solar metallicity ($Z/Z_\odot < 0.01$) exists due to the lack of detectable iron lines and subtle continuum curvature below $40\text{ keV}$.
citation_leads: III.1 Spectral analysis: “The subtle continuum curvature below 40 keV makes it difficult to unambiguously decouple a very high $kT_{\max}$ from an extremely low metallicity ($Z/Z_{\odot}<0.01$), which is required to suppress the H- and He-like iron lines.”

III.2 Timing analysis: “Despite the transition from a nuclear-burning SSS phase to an accretion-powered quiescent state, the pulse minima show a remarkably small phase shift. This stability indicates that the magnetic poles remained the primary site of both”
V Conclusions: “By folding both the 2021 and 2024 light curves with the same spin ephemeris, we found that the pulse minima are aligned.”
